target.title: fix(doctor): bound session snapshot store reads with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor session-snapshot scan/repair loaded session store JSON with unbounded
`fs.readFileSync` at two call sites. A corrupted or hostile multi-GB
`sessions.json` under the user state directory could OOM `openclaw doctor`
before JSON parse or repair logic ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a shared `readSnapshotStoreRaw` helper with `statSync` +
`MAX_SNAPSHOT_STORE_BYTES = 16 MiB`, and route both the scan loader and the
repair backup read through it. Oversized stores fail closed: doctor emits an
operator-visible Session snapshots note, structured health issues use
`kind: "store-too-large"`, and repair effects record
`would-skip-oversized-session-store`.

## User Impact

**Before:** An oversized session store could force an unbounded sync string
alloc during doctor snapshot health, or be skipped silently with no operator
signal.

**After:** Stores above 16 MiB are rejected before `readFileSync`. Doctor
reports the skip, and normal stores continue to scan/repair.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.ts`,
  `src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts`
- Production path: `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` /
  `noteSessionSnapshotHealth` → `loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` /
  repair `updateSessionStore` callback → `readSnapshotStoreRaw`
- Compatibility: normal stores unchanged; oversized stores are skipped with a
  warning instead of crashing the process

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

A ~17 MiB session store is not passed to `readFileSync`. Isolated
`openclaw doctor --non-interactive --yes` prints a Session snapshots note that
the store was skipped as oversized.

### Canonical reachability path

`openclaw doctor` → session snapshot health →
`noteSessionSnapshotHealth` / `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` →
`loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` → `readSnapshotStoreRaw` (stat + 16 MiB cap)
→ skip + warn on overflow

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Same bound pattern as other doctor store caps; no new config/env keys.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; Node 22.23.1; isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `HOME` under `/tmp` with a
planted 17 MiB `sessions.json`; CLI via
`node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes` after local build.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
PROOF=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-doctor-snap-proof-XXXXXX)
STATE=$PROOF/state; HOME_DIR=$PROOF/home; CONFIG=$PROOF/openclaw.json
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR" "$STATE/agents/main/sessions"
printf '%s\n' '{"agents":{"list":[{"id":"main","default":true}]}}' > "$CONFIG"
# write 17 MiB of bytes to $STATE/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
HOME=$HOME_DIR OPENCLAW_HOME=$HOME_DIR OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE \
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$CONFIG CI=true \
  node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes
```

Focused regression:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts \
  -t "oversized session stores" --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Redacted CLI:

```text
◇  Session snapshots ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - Skipped oversized session store                                                    │
│    .../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json                                       │
│    (.../sessions.json: file too large (17825792 bytes, max 16777216)).                │
│    Snapshot-path health was not scanned.                                              │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Focused tests:

```text
✓ reports oversized session stores without reading them into memory
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 24 skipped (25)
```

### Observed result after fix

Real `openclaw doctor` warns and skips the oversized store; `readFileSync` is
never called for that path during snapshot scan.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.
